positive: A ready Phase 2A.1 resolution receipt can be projected into a content-addressed immutable pack under .tailtrail/official-aidlc/packs without changing the verified source bundle.

Provisioning uses one bounded cross-platform OS lock at .tailtrail/official-aidlc/locks/provision.lock, rechecks destination state after acquisition, stages on the destination filesystem, validates every copied byte, and atomically renames only into an absent destination.

A closed versioned projection receipt separately binds the source resolution fingerprint, source and project inventories, immutable pack identity, trust posture, creation result, and project projection fingerprint.
A closed versioned current.json selector is atomically created for future runs only and binds the exact immutable pack and projection receipt fingerprints.

Repeated provisioning of the same valid bundle returns reused without rewriting pack files, changing their modification times, appending duplicate projection events, or replacing an identical selector.
Concurrent provisioning produces one created result and one reused result without exposing a partial pack.

An explicit bounded recovery operation can remove only a named stale staging directory created under the managed packs root; ordinary provisioning reports pre-existing staging state and does not silently clean it.

Focused proof covers successful creation, idempotent reuse, selector stability, lock timeout and release, concurrent calls, interrupted staging recovery, deep target roots, and negative destination states.
negative: Provisioning never contacts the network, executes bundle content, mutates the source bundle, follows symlinks, writes outside the target .tailtrail directory, or weakens the Phase 2A.1 trust posture.
A missing, altered, incomplete, incompatible, unsafe, or occupied content-addressed destination blocks without overwrite, deletion, selector replacement, or automatic repair.
An existing selector for a different pack blocks until a separately approved migration; Phase 2A.2 never retargets an active run or treats current.json as an active-run binding.
Unknown filesystem errors fail immediately; retries are bounded and limited to explicitly recognized transient rename contention.

This slice does not edit generic installer helpers, public detector or installer scripts, Requirements lookup, Full Start routing, Planning Lock attachment, MCP routing, host adapters, schemas, package registration, or documentation.
